BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r1.claim: The Prophet received knowledge without learning to write and became a source of knowledge about writing, its rules, and crafts; God knows what is manifest and hidden.
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r1.anchor: من غير تعلم الخط وكان منبع الكمالات كلها حتى إنه علم الكتاب الخط وقوانينه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r1.claim: God promises the unlettered Prophet a clear sign: Gabriel recites revelation and he retains it, except what God abrogates by removing its ruling and recitation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r1.anchor: أن يقرأ عليه جبريل ما يقرأ عليه من الوحي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r2.claim: Another explanation says the Prophet hurried to repeat Gabriel's recitation, so he was told to wait for repeated instruction and would remember after any lapse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r2.anchor: كان يعجل بالقراءة إذا لقنه جبريل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r3.claim: The exception may mean rare lapses: a report says he omitted a verse during prayer, and Ubayy thought it had been abrogated before the Prophet said he had forgotten it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r3.anchor: أنه أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the exception is a rhetorical affirmation of no forgetting, or the verse prohibits neglecting repeated recitation with an extra alif for rhyme; God may cause forgetting by abrogating recitation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r4.anchor: الغرض نفى النسيان رأسا كما يقول الرجل لصاحبه أنت سهيمي فيما أملك إلا فيما شاء الله ولا يقصد استثناء شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r1.claim: The exception means God may cause the Prophet to forget recitation by lifting its recitation for a benefit; the author prefers this because the exception from a prohibition is normally temporary and the yāʾ appears in every codex and reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r1.anchor: والأول هو المختار لأن الاستثناء من النهي لا يكاد يكون إلا مؤقتا معلوما

QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r2.claim: Other explanations say the exception means God may defer revelation, or that pasture does not become debris when humans or animals use it.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه إلا ما شاء الله أن يؤخر إنزاله.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r7.claim: One interpretation says God informs the Prophet that He will teach and preserve the Qurʾān, while telling him not to rush its recitation.
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هذا إخبار من الله نبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه يعلمه هذا القرآن، ويحفظه عليه، ونهي منه أن يعجل بقراءته

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r1.speaker: قائلو هذه المقالة
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r1.claim: This interpretation reads the exception as allowing God to cause the Prophet to forget what He abrogates, removing its ruling and recitation.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r1.anchor: فقال قائلو هذه المقالة: معنى الاستثناء في هذا الموضع على النسيان، ومعنى الكلام: فلا تنسى، إلا ما شاء الله أن تنساه

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet would rehearse the Qurʾān within himself from fear of forgetting it.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: " {سنقرئك فلا تنسى} [سورة:] قال: كان يتذكر القرآن في نفسه مخافة أن ينسى "

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r3.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet forgot nothing except what God willed him to forget.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، " {سنقرئك فلا تنسى} كان صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا {إلا ما شاء الله} [الأنعام: 128] "

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r4.claim: Another interpretation reads forgetting as leaving Qurʾānic practice, except where God abrogates a ruling.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى النسيان في هذا الموضع: الترك؛ وقالوا: معنى الكلام: سنقرئك يا محمد فلا تترك العمل بشيء منه

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r5.claim: Some grammarians say God did not will the Prophet to forget anything; the exception is an idiomatic oath-like formula whose intent is to give everything requested.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r5.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يقول في ذلك: لم يشأ الله أن تنسى شيئا، وهو كقوله: {خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك}

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r6.claim: Ṭabarī prefers that the exception means God may cause the Prophet to forget through abrogation and removal, judging this the clearest sense.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r6.anchor: والقول الذي هو أولى بالصواب عندي، قول من قال: معنى ذلك: فلا تنسى إلا أن نشاء نحن أن ننسيكه بنسخه ورفعه.

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet feared forgetting the Qurʾān until God assured him he would recite without forgetting.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r9.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يستذكر القرآن مخافة أن ينساه

TABRISI:87:7-9/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r8.claim: Iqraʾ is receiving a reading by listening to correct errors; qāriʾ also means one who recites, from gathering letters together.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r8.anchor: والإقراء أخذ القراءة على القارىء بالاستماع لتقويم الزلل والقارىء التالي

TABRISI:87:7-9/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r9.claim: Forgetting is loss of meaning from the mind, like absent-mindedness; it contrasts with remembrance and is not simply loss of acquired knowledge.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r9.anchor: والنسيان ذهاب المعنى عن النفس ونظيره السهو ونقيضه الذكر

TABRISI:87:7-9/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r10.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:87:7-9/r10.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says forgetting is an act of God.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r10.anchor: وقال أبو علي الجبائي: وهو معنى من فعل الله تعالى

TABRISI:87:7/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r20.claim: God will make the Prophet recite the Qurʾān so that he does not forget it; alternatively Gabriel recites it by God's command and he retains it.
TABRISI:87:7/r20.anchor: أي سنأخذ عليك قراءة القرآن فلا تنسى ذلك

TABRISI:87:7/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:87:7/r21.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet used to repeat Gabriel's revelation for fear of forgetting, but after this verse he forgot nothing.
TABRISI:87:7/r21.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه جبرائيل ع بالوحي يقرأه مخافة أن ينساه

THALABI:v10p183#2/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r17.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p183#2/r17.claim: Qatāda takes the exception to forgetting as whatever God chooses to abrogate from the Qurʾān; ‘We shall make you recite’ means teach you through Gabriel's recitation.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r17.anchor: سنقرئك: سنعلمك ويقرأ عليك جبريل، فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله أن تنساه

BURHAN:v4p297/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p297/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v4p297/r6.claim: Some grammarians distinguish a conditional answer that follows causally from one that stands in the place of an unstated consequence; these examples illustrate causality.
BURHAN:v4p297/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم إذا ترتب الجواب بالفاء

BURHAN:v4p353/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p353/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p353/r1.claim: The negative particle la can negate the speaker's or addressee's present or future action; it can also enter past-tense oath or prayer formulas and ordinary past clauses.
BURHAN:v4p353/r1.anchor: والنفي بها يتناول فعل المتكلم نحو لا أخرج اليوم ولا أسافر غدا

BURHAN:v1p237/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p237/r1.speaker: الحاكم
BURHAN:v1p237/r1.claim: Al-Hakim says Quran collection occurred in stages: some in the Prophet’s presence, another under Abu Bakr, and the third, ordering surahs, under Uthman.
BURHAN:v1p237/r1.anchor: وفيه البيان الواضح أن جمع القرآن لم يكن مرة واحدة فقد جمع بعضه بحضرة النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURHAN:v1p237/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p237/r2.speaker: المحاسبي
BURHAN:v1p237/r2.claim: Al-Muhasibi says writing began by the Prophet’s command on separate materials; Abu Bakr ordered the fragments copied together and tied so none would be lost.
BURHAN:v1p237/r2.anchor: كتابة القرآن ليست محدثة فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يأمر بكتابته ولكنه كان مفرقا فى الرقاع والأكتاف والعسب

BURHAN:v1p237/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p237/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p237/r3.claim: The collectors trusted fragments and reciters because the community knew the Quran’s miraculous composition and had witnessed its recitation for twenty years; the danger was loss, not additions.
BURHAN:v1p237/r3.anchor: لأنهم كانوا يبدون عن تأليف معجز ونظم معروف وقد شاهدوا تلاوته من النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم عشرين سنة

BURHAN:v1p237/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p237/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p237/r4.claim: The Prophet did not need a collected codex because God secured him from forgetfulness, except what He willed to abrogate; collection became necessary when people feared forgetting.
BURHAN:v1p237/r4.anchor: لأن الله تعالى كان قد أمنه من النسيان بقوله ﴿ سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله ﴾ أن يرفع حكمه بالنسخ

BURHAN:v1p237/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p237/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p237/r5.claim: Zayd’s report of collecting fragments does not mean no Quran had been gathered during the Prophet’s life; he checked scattered material against memorizers so the community could be sure nothing was missing.
BURHAN:v1p237/r5.anchor: وإنما طلب القرآن متفرقا ليعارض بالمجتمع عند من بقى ممن جمع القرآن ليشترك الجميع فى علم ما جمع

ITQAN:v4p430/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p430/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p430/r10.claim: Suyuti says the opening is travel-revealed; permission to fight abrogates the judgment verse, which the sword verse superseded, and the passage beginning “We sent before you” is abrogated by 87:6.
ITQAN:v4p430/r10.anchor: قلت والسفري أولها والناسخ ﴿ أذن للذين يقاتلون ﴾ الآية والمنسوخ ﴿ الله يحكم بينكم ﴾ الآية نسختها آية السيف وقوله ﴿ وما أرسلنا من قبلك ﴾ نسختها ﴿ سنقرئك فلا تنسى ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p453/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r11.claim: Here tansā means retaining or remembering the recitation permanently; the same root can mean failing to remember something.
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r11.anchor: الثاني نسي أي لم يحفظ قوله تعالى في سورة الأعلى سنقرئك فلا تنسى أي تحفظ فلا تنساه البتة

DAMGHANI:v1p426/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p426/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p426/r1.claim: Lā can mark an asserted negation, as in the statement that the Prophet will not forget.
DAMGHANI:v1p426/r1.anchor: الثالث : لا بمعنى الخبر . قوله تعالى فى سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r2.claim: One Qur'anic use is negation, as in God's not speaking to people and the promise that the Prophet will not forget.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن ' لا ' في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p579#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p579#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p579#2/r1.claim: Nisyān with kasra nūn and sukūn sīn is distinguished from the form with both vowels open, called the twin of the sciatic nerve.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p579#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p579#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p579#2/r4.claim: Nisyān can mean the opposite of remembering.

NASHR:v1p454/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p454/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p454/r3.claim: For a hamza with ḍamma after kasra, as in wa-lā yunabbiʾuka and sanaqriʾuka, the rasm uses yāʾ according to al-Akhfash rather than the customary waw.
NASHR:v1p454/r3.anchor: فلم يرسم على مذهب الجادة بواو، بل رسم على مذهب الأخفش بالياء

NASHR:v1p444/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p444/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p444/r1.claim: Al-Dānī says the method attributed by Khalaf to al-Kisāʾī has no practical basis; the author rejects al-Shāṭibī’s allusion to it as unsupported by transmission or analogy.
NASHR:v1p444/r1.anchor: وحكاه خلف عن الكسائي، قال الداني: وهذا لا عمل عليه.

NASHR:v1p444/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p444/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p444/r2.claim: Al-Dānī and the majority attribute to al-Akhfash substitution of a hamza after kasra or ḍamma with yāʾ or wāw, including forms such as سنقريك and اللؤلؤ.
NASHR:v1p444/r2.anchor: فقال الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني في جامعه: هذا هو مذهب الأخفش النحوي الذي لا يجوز عنده غيره.

NASHR:v1p444/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p444/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p444/r3.claim: The author says al-Akhfash’s own book only permits substitution when the hamza is the word’s final radical; for medial or separate-word cases he uses Sibawayh’s between-between easing.
NASHR:v1p444/r3.anchor: إلا إذا كانت الهمزة لام الفعل نحو (سنقريك، واللولو)

NASHR:v1p444/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p444/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p444/r4.claim: Readers and grammarians commonly report al-Akhfash’s substitution rule for both categories; Abū al-ʿIzz also permits it for Ḥamza at pause.
NASHR:v1p444/r4.anchor: والذي يحكيه عنه القراء والنحاة إطلاق الإبدال في النوعين، وأجازه كذلك عن حمزة في الوقف أبو العز القلانسي وغيره،

NASHR:v1p444/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p444/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p444/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ permits substitution of a hamza with ḍamma after kasra across connected or separate words; Abū al-ʿIzz reports regional variation, including between-between easing.
NASHR:v1p444/r5.anchor: فقط مطلقا، أي: في المنفصل والمتصل فاء الفعل ولامه

NASHR:v1p445/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p445/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p445/r1.claim: Some authorities rejected al-Akhfash’s method in the work وقف حمزة, while others adopted a distinction based on agreement with the muṣḥaf’s rasm.
NASHR:v1p445/r1.anchor: الأخفش، ورد عليه في كتابه وقف حمزة، وذهب آخرون من الأئمة إلى التفصيل

NASHR:v1p445/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p445/r2.speaker: الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p445/r2.claim: Another group follows al-Akhfash where the written form supports it, as in سنقريك and اللؤلؤ, but follows Sibawayh for forms such as سئل and يستهزؤون; al-Dānī chooses this distinction.
NASHR:v1p445/r2.anchor: وهو اختيار الحافظ أبي عمرو الداني وغيره

NASHR:v1p445/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p445/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p445/r3.claim: Some grammarians report that non-Ḥijāzī Arabs pause on final hamza by replacing it with a vowel letter: wāw in nominative, yāʾ in genitive, and alif in accusative.
NASHR:v1p445/r3.anchor: وذهب جماعة من النحاة إلى جواز إبدال الهمزة المتطرفة في الوقف من جنس حركتها في الوصل

NASHR:v1p445/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p445/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p445/r4.claim: When the replacement follows the hamza’s own vowel, pause signs such as rawm or ishāmām remain possible; when it follows the preceding consonant’s vowel, they are not.
NASHR:v1p445/r4.anchor: وتظهر فائدة الخلاف في الإشارة بالروم والإشمام، ففي تخفيفها بحركة نفسها تأتي الإشارة،

NASHR:v1p445/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p445/r5.speaker: أبو الفتح فارس بن أحمد
NASHR:v1p445/r5.claim: Some readers apply the pause form that matches the written muṣḥaf; Abū al-Fatḥ and al-Dānī favor this, following wāw, yāʾ, or alif as written.
NASHR:v1p445/r5.anchor: وهذا مذهب أبي الفتح فارس بن أحمد وغيره، واختيار الحافظ أبي عمرو

ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومالك
ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and Mālik connect this promise to the instruction not to move the tongue hastily; God preserves the revelation for the unlettered Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r1.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة ومالك : هذا في معنى { لا تحرك به لسانك } وعده الله أن يقرئه ، وأخبره أنه لا ينسى ، وهذه آية للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم في أنه أمّيّ ، وحفظ الله عليه الوحي

ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r2.claim: Another view treats the verse as a promise to recite the sūras and a confirming command not to forget; since forgetting is not in his power, it warns him not to neglect review.
ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r2.anchor: وقيل : هذا وعد بإقراء السور ، وأمر أن لا ينسى على معنى التثبيت والتأكيد ، وقد علم أن النسيان ليس في قدرته ، فهو نهي عن إغفال التعاهد

ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r3.claim: The alif remains in falā tansā despite the jussive prohibition particle, to regularize the verse endings.
ABUHAYYAN:87:6/r3.anchor: وأثبتت الألف في { فلا تنسى } ، وإن كان مجزوماً بلا التي للنهي لتعديل رءوس الآي .

ALUSI:87:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r1.claim: This is the Messenger’s special guidance, following the account of God’s general guidance to all creatures.
ALUSI:87:6/r1.anchor: بيان لهدايته تعالى شأنه الخاصة برسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أثر بيان هدايته عز وجل العامة لكافة مخلوقاته سبحانه

ALUSI:87:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r2.claim: The special guidance is receiving and memorizing the Qurʾān, itself guidance for all worlds, and being enabled to guide all people.
ALUSI:87:6/r2.anchor: وهي هدايته عليه الصلاة والسلام لتلقي الوحي وحفظ القرآن الذي هو هدى للعالمين وتوفيقه صلى الله عليه وسلم لهداية الناس أجمعين

ALUSI:87:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r3.claim: The future tense may emphasize the promise, or refer to revelation already received and yet to come, promising its continuation.
ALUSI:87:6/r3.anchor: والسين إما للتأكيد وإما لأن المراد إقراء ما أوحي إليه صلى الله عليه وسلم حينئذ وما سيوحي إليه عليه الصلاة والسلام بعد

ALUSI:87:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r4.claim: “We shall make you recite” is attributed to God metaphorically: Gabriel mediates the revelation in all its modes.
ALUSI:87:6/r4.anchor: وإسناد الإقراء إليه تعالى مجازي أي سنقرئك ما نوحي إليك الآن وفيما بعد على لسان جبريل

ALUSI:87:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r5.claim: The Prophet will not forget the Qurʾān because of his strong retention and precision; this is a sign alongside the Qurʾān’s inimitability and reports of the unseen, especially given his being unlettered.
ALUSI:87:6/r5.anchor: فلا تنسى أصلاً من قوة الحفظ والإتقان مع أنك أمي لم تكن تدري ما الكتاب وما القراءة ليكون ذلك لك آية

ALUSI:87:6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r6.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ALUSI:87:6/r6.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq is cited for the possibility that the Prophet could read writing without anyone teaching him, while he did not write.
ALUSI:87:6/r6.anchor: فقد روي عن جعفر الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يقرأ الكتابة ولا يكتب

ALUSI:87:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r7.claim: A view takes “you will not forget” as an absolute divine favor of perfect memory, but al-Ālūsī says this conflicts with early transmitted interpretation and with the consequential fāʾ.
ALUSI:87:6/r7.anchor: ويكون المراد بقوله تعالى فلا تنسى نفي النسيان مطلقاً عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام امتناناً عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم بأنه أوتي قوة الحفظ

ALUSI:87:6/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r8.claim: Another view means the Prophet will not neglect the Qurʾān’s content in practice, a promise to follow its rulings; al-Ālūsī calls this far-fetched.
ALUSI:87:6/r8.anchor: وجوز أيضاً أن يكون المراد نفي نسيان المضمون أي سنقرئك القرآن فلا تغفل عنه فتخالفه في أعمالك

ALUSI:87:6/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:6/r9.claim: A view construes “do not forget” as a prohibition and treats the final alif as rhyme, as in 33:67; its problem is that forgetfulness is involuntary.
ALUSI:87:6/r9.anchor: وقيل فلا تنسى نهى والألف لمراعاة الفاصلة كما في قوله تعالى

ALUSI:87:6/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r10.claim: The prohibition can only be rescued by making it figurative—avoid voluntary causes of forgetting or do not act against the recited message—which adds strain without cause.
ALUSI:87:6/r10.anchor: إلا أن يراد مجازاً ترك أسبابه الاختيارية أو ترك العمل بما تضمنه المقرأ وفيه ارتكاب تكلف من غير داع

ALUSI:87:6/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r11.claim: Some say the final alif was written as yāʾ to match the rhyme and its original form; al-Marzūqī says a deleted alif is restored in pausal recitation.
ALUSI:87:6/r11.anchor: نعم قيل رسمت ألف الاطلاق ياء لموافقة غيرها من الفواصل وموافقة أصلها مع أن الإمام المرزوقي صرح بأنه عند الاطلاق ترد المحذوفة

ALUSI:87:6/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r12.claim: Another prohibitive analysis keeps the alif because a jussive may leave a weak letter, but al-Ālūsī also finds this unsatisfactory.
ALUSI:87:6/r12.anchor: وقيل هو نهى لكن لم تحذف الألف فيه إذ قد لا يحذف الجازم حرف العلة وحسن ذلك هنا مراعاة الفاصلة

ALUSI:87:6/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:6/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:6/r13.claim: The easiest prohibition reading for students treats the statement as a report intended to prohibit one of the voluntary kinds of forgetting described above.
ALUSI:87:6/r13.anchor: والأهون للطالب معنى النهي أن يقول هو خبر أريد به النهي على أحد التأويلين السابقين آنفاً

BAGHAWI:87:6/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:6/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:6/r1.claim: “We shall make you recite” means God will teach the Prophet through Gabriel reciting to him.

BAYDAWI:87:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:6/r1.claim: God will have Gabriel recite to the Prophet, or will make him a reciter through inspired reading.
BAYDAWI:87:6/r1.anchor: سنقرئك على لسان جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام أو سنجعلك قارئا بإلهام القراءة

BAYDAWI:87:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:6/r2.claim: The Prophet will forget nothing because of his powerful memory; this is another sign despite his being unlettered, and the prediction's fulfillment is itself a sign.
BAYDAWI:87:6/r2.anchor: فلا تنسى أصلا من قوة الحفظ مع أنك أمي ليكون ذلك آية أخرى لك

BAYDAWI:87:6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:6/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes the phrase as a prohibition; the final alif marks the verse ending, as in 17:67.
BAYDAWI:87:6/r3.anchor: وقيل نهي والألف للفاصلة كقوله تعالى السبيلا

BIQAI:87:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:6/r1.claim: After completing the account of the Creator's attributes and acts, the sūra turns to creatures, beginning with the Prophet and prophethood, which completes felicity through revealed truth and the intellectual and practical powers.
BIQAI:87:6/r1.anchor: فتم ما للخالق ، أتبعه ما للخلائق

BIQAI:87:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:6/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:6/r2.claim: Human flourishing requires an exemplar in speech, action, and conduct; none compares with the one protected from deviation, and love for God's sake is a chief support of religion.
BIQAI:87:6/r2.anchor: مثل المعصوم عن كل ميل الموجب ذلك الحب

BIQAI:87:6/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:6/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:6/r3.claim: God promises repeated, ongoing instruction in this life-giving revelation: He will make the unlettered Prophet a reader who knows it fully and conveys it among people.
BIQAI:87:6/r3.anchor: أي نجعلك بعظمتنا بوعد لا خلف فيه على سبيل التكرار بالتجديد والاستمرار قارئاً

BIQAI:87:6/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:6/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:6/r4.claim: The revelation separates confused matters and revives dead spirits through knowledge as God revives dead bodies through souls.
BIQAI:87:6/r4.anchor: أنه يحيي ميت الأرواح بالعلم كما يحيي ميت الأشباح بالأرواح

BIQAI:87:6/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:6/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:6/r5.claim: God ensures the Prophet will forget nothing of this revelation or anything else.
BIQAI:87:6/r5.anchor: أي شيئاً منه ولا من غيره ليكون في ذلك آيتان

BIQAI:87:6/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:6/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:6/r6.claim: His reading despite being unlettered and his true prediction of future events are two signs; he should not strain to hurry the recitation, since God preserves it in his heart and enables his tongue.
BIQAI:87:6/r6.anchor: ليكون في ذلك آيتان : كونك تقرأ وأنت أمي ، وكونك تخبر عن المستقبل

DURR:87:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:6/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:87:6/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet rehearsed the Qurʾān internally because he feared forgetting it.
DURR:87:6/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : { سنقرئك فلا تنسى } قال : كان يتذكر القرآن في نفسه مخافة أن ينسى .

DURR:87:6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts the Prophet’s fear of forgetting revelation, Gabriel’s reassurance, the promise of preservation except what God willed, forgotten or lifted non-legal verses, and Moses’ broken tablets.
DURR:87:6/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه جبريل بالوحي لم يفرغ جبريل من الوحي

DURR:87:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:6/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet reviewed the Qurʾān fearing to forget; he was told it would be taken care of and the verse was revealed.
DURR:87:6/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستذكر القرآن

DURR:87:6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:6/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
DURR:87:6/r4.claim: Al-Ḥākim reports a similar account from Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ.
DURR:87:6/r4.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم عن سعد بن أبي وقاص نحوه .

IBNASHUR:87:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:6/r1.claim: The opening command’s implicit good news is stated directly here: God pledges to preserve what He recites to the Prophet so he can convey it as revealed.
IBNASHUR:87:6/r1.anchor: فهذا موقع البيان الصريح بوعده بأنه سيعصمه من نسيان ما يقرئه فيبلغه كما أوحي إليه

IBNASHUR:87:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:87:6/r2.claim: Citing Ibn Abbas as a sound report, Ibn Ashur recounts that the Prophet moved his lips and tongue during revelation, fearing it would slip from memory; God instructed him to listen while Gabriel recited and promised to gather the Quran in his heart.
IBNASHUR:87:6/r2.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيح عن ابن عباس : « أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يعالج من التنزيل شدة

IBNASHUR:87:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:6/r3.claim: Because al-Qiyamah, which contains the instruction not to hurry the tongue, came later, this earlier verse promises God’s help in preserving all revelation.
IBNASHUR:87:6/r3.anchor: نزلت بعد سورة الأعلى فقد تعين أن قوله

IBNASHUR:87:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:6/r4.claim: God first promises to recite to the Prophet, preparing for the main assurance that he will not forget; the Quran will keep growing, yet its preservation is assured.
IBNASHUR:87:6/r4.anchor: فإذا كان قد خاف من نسيان بعض ما أوحي إليه على حين قلته فإنه سيتتابع

IBNASHUR:87:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:6/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:6/r5.claim: The prefixed sīn marks futurity and, with an action already underway, signals continuing, renewed recitation and so strengthens the assurance.
IBNASHUR:87:6/r5.anchor: والسين علامة على استقبال مدخولها ، وهي تفيد تأكيد حصول الفعل

IBNASHUR:87:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:6/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:6/r6.claim: The shift to the majestic first-person plural makes direct address more fitting for the giver of good news.
IBNASHUR:87:6/r6.anchor: والالتفات بضمير المتكلم المعظم لأن التكلم أنسب بالإقبال على المبشر

IBNASHUR:87:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:6/r7.claim: Attributing the recitation to God is a rational metaphor: He brings about the recited speech and commands it to be recited.
IBNASHUR:87:6/r7.anchor: وإسناد الإقراء إلى الله مجاز عقلي لأنه جاعل الكلام المقروء وآمر بإقرائه

IBNASHUR:87:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:6/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:6/r8.claim: The statement that the Prophet will not forget is phrased as a report but functions as a promise and guarantee.
IBNASHUR:87:6/r8.anchor: فقوله : { فلا تنسى } خبر مراد به الوعد والتكفل له بذلك

IBNASHUR:87:6/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:6/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:6/r9.claim: Forgetting is when information previously known fails to come to mind for a while, whether briefly or for a long time.
IBNASHUR:87:6/r9.anchor: والنسيان : عدم خطور المعلوم السابق في حافظة الإنسان برهة أو زماناً طويلاً

IBNATIYYA:87:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومالك ابن أنس
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r1.claim: They link this promise to 75:16: the Prophet moved his lips hastily for fear of forgetting, but God promised preservation so no verse would be irretrievably lost, a sign of preserving revelation to an unlettered Prophet.
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r1.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة ومالك ابن أنس : هذه الآية في معنى قوله تعالى : { لا تحرك به لسانك } [ القيامة : 16 ]

IBNATIYYA:87:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r2.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r2.claim: Others distinguish it from 75:16: it promises the preservation of the law and sūras and reinforces the command not to forget; since forgetting is not fully under one's control, the Prophet is still told not to neglect review.
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون : ليست هذه الآية في معنى تلك ، وإنما هذه وعد بإقرار الشرع والسور ، وأمره أن لا ينسى على معنى التثبيت والتأكيد

IBNATIYYA:87:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r3.claim: The final yāʾ in tansā is written to maintain the rhyme at the verse endings.
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r3.anchor: وأثبت الياء في «تنسى » لتعديل رؤوس الآي

IBNATIYYA:87:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r4.speaker: الجنيد
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r4.claim: Al-Junayd interprets “do not forget” as “do not abandon acting on its commands and prohibitions.”
IBNATIYYA:87:6/r4.anchor: وقال الجنيد : معنى { فلا تنسى } ، لا تترك العمل بما تضمن من أمر ونهي

IBNKATHIR:87:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r1.claim: God promises Muhammad that He will teach him the recitation so that he will not forget it, except what God wills.
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r1.anchor: وهذا إخبار من الله ، عز وجل ، ووعد منه له ، بأنه سيقرئه قراءة لا ينساها

IBNKATHIR:87:6/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r2.claim: Ibn Jarīr chooses the reading that the Prophet will not forget what God recites to him except what God wills.
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r2.anchor: إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ } وهذا اختيار ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR:87:6/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r3.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet would forget nothing except what God willed.
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا إلا ما شاء الله

IBNKATHIR:87:6/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r4.claim: An alternative takes “do not forget” as a command: the exception concerns material God abrogates, which the Prophet may then leave without blame.
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r4.anchor: وقيل : المراد بقوله : { فَلا تَنْسَى } طلب ، وجعلوا معنى الاستثناء على هذا ما يقع من النسخ

MAWARDI:87:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:6/r1.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:6/r1.claim: One interpretation takes do not forget to mean do not abandon the work, except where God grants a concession; on this reading the phrase prohibits associating partners with God.
MAWARDI:87:6/r1.anchor: أن معنى قوله : فلا تنسى ،   أي فلا تترك العمل إلا ما شاء الله أن يترخص لك فيه ،   فعلى هذا التأويل يكون هذا نهياً عن الشرك

MAWARDI:87:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:6/r2.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:6/r2.claim: The other interpretation is God’s assurance that the Prophet will not forget the Qur’an He recites to him.
MAWARDI:87:6/r2.anchor: أنه إخبار من الله تعالى أنه لا ينسى ما يقرئه من القرآن

MAWARDI:87:6/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:87:6/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that the Prophet repeated Gabriel’s revelation for fear of forgetting, so God revealed that He would recite the Qur’an to him and he would not forget; no grading is given.
MAWARDI:87:6/r3.anchor:
حكى ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا نزل عليه جبريل بالوحي يقرؤه خيفة أن ينساه ،   فأنزل الله تعالى :
"  سنقرئك فلا تنسى

NASAFI:87:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:6/r1.claim: Nasafi glosses the promise as God teaching the Prophet the Qur’an until he forgets it, using that wording in his explanation of the assurance against forgetting.
NASAFI:87:6/r1.anchor: سنقرئك فلا تنسى } سنعلمك القرآن حتى تنساه

QURTUBI:87:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:6/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI:87:6/r1.claim: Malik explains “We shall make you recite” as teaching Muhammad the Quran and “you will not forget” as “you will retain it”; Ibn Wahb transmits this.
QURTUBI:87:6/r1.anchor: أي فتحفظ ، رواه ابن وهب عن مالك

QURTUBI:87:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:6/r2.claim: This is divine good news: though unlettered and unable to read or write, Muhammad will hear Gabriel recite revelation and memorize it without forgetting.
QURTUBI:87:6/r2.anchor: وهذه بشرى من الله تعالى ، بشره بأن أعطاه آية بينة

QURTUBI:87:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:6/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:87:6/r3.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet reviewed revelation for fear of forgetting and was told God would preserve it; Ibn Abi Najih transmits this.
QURTUBI:87:6/r3.anchor: وعن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ، قال : كان يتذكر مخافة أن ينسى

QURTUBI:87:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:6/r4.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
QURTUBI:87:6/r4.claim: Mujahid and al-Kalbi say Muhammad began repeating a verse before Gabriel finished reciting it, fearing loss; revelation promised he would not forget and relieved him of that fear.
QURTUBI:87:6/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد والكلبي : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه جبريل بالوحي

RAZI:87:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r1.claim: After commanding glorification, God assures the Prophet because complete glorification requires reciting the revealed Qur’an, and he feared forgetting it.
RAZI:87:6/r1.anchor: لما أمر محمدا بالتسبيح فقال : { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى }

RAZI:87:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r2.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:87:6/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains “We shall make you recite” as inspiring the Prophet to read and ensuring he does not forget what he reads.
RAZI:87:6/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي : { سنقرئك } أي سنجعلك قارئا

RAZI:87:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI:87:6/r3.claim: Mujāhid, Muqātil, and al-Kalbī report that the Prophet moved his tongue rapidly during revelation from fear of forgetting, before Gabriel had finished reciting.
RAZI:87:6/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد ومقاتل والكلبي : كان عليه السلام إذا نزل عليه القرآن

RAZI:87:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r4.claim: One explanation is that Gabriel will read the Qur’an to the Prophet repeatedly until he memorizes it without forgetting.
RAZI:87:6/r4.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام سيقرأ عليك القرآن مرات حتى تحفظه حفظا لا تنساه

RAZI:87:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r5.claim: Another explanation is that God will expand the Prophet’s heart and strengthen his resolve so that one reading suffices for lasting memorization.
RAZI:87:6/r5.anchor: أنا نشرح صدرك ونقوي خاطرك حتى تحفظ بالمرة الواحدة حفظا لا تنساه

RAZI:87:6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r6.claim: A third explanation links the promise to the opening command: persist in glorification, and God will gather the Qur’an’s knowledge in the Prophet’s heart and ease him to act on it.
RAZI:87:6/r6.anchor: واظب على ذلك ودم عليه فإنا سنقرئك القرآن الجامع لعلوم الأولين والآخرين

RAZI:87:6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r7.claim: The verse demonstrates prophethood: an unlettered man retained a long scripture without study, repetition, or writing, beyond ordinary capacity.
RAZI:87:6/r7.anchor: كان رجلا أميا فحفظه لهذا الكتاب المطول من غير دراسة ولا تكرار ولا كتبة

RAZI:87:6/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r8.claim: Because this early Meccan sūra predicts an extraordinary future event that occurred, the promise is foreknowledge and a miracle.
RAZI:87:6/r8.anchor: أن هذه السورة من أوائل ما نزل بمكة

RAZI:87:6/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r9.claim: Some read the phrase as a prohibition, treating the final alif as rhyme; the Prophet must not neglect reciting and reviewing, lest he forget except what God wills.
RAZI:87:6/r9.anchor: قال بعضهم : { فلا تنسى } معناه النهي

RAZI:87:6/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r10.claim: The well-known reading is a promise: God will teach the Prophet until he is secure from forgetting, as one might promise clothing so someone will not remain unclothed.
RAZI:87:6/r10.anchor: والقول المشهور أن هذا خبر والمعنى سنقرئك إلى أن تصير بحيث لا تنسى وتأمن النسيان

RAZI:87:6/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r11.claim: Rāzī considers the prohibitive reading weaker: it requires an irregular added alif and makes the verse a command to use study and review rather than a divine promise.
RAZI:87:6/r11.anchor: على خلاف قوله : { لا تحرك به لسانك

RAZI:87:6/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:6/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:87:6/r12.claim: Rāzī adds that forgetfulness is under God’s control, so a prohibition against it must be indirect; the promise gives greater reassurance and honor.
RAZI:87:6/r12.anchor: ذلك القول لا يتم إلا عند التزام مجازات في هذه الآية منها أن النسيان لا يقدر عليه إلا الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r1.claim: Worldly ornaments, pleasures, food, and drink perish quickly like withered debris; attachment distracts from special glorification and veils each person's potential perfection.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r1.anchor: مرعى النفس الحيوانية ومرتع بهائم القوى جعلها الله سريعة الفناء وشيكة الزوال

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r2.claim: Worldly life obstructs the special glorification that strips the divine essence of attachments.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r2.anchor: فإنها مانعة عن التسبيح الخاص وهو تنزيه الذات وتجريدها عن العلائق

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r3.claim: The verse describes God's special guidance of the Messenger, following His general guidance to all creatures.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r3.anchor: بيان لهدايته تعالى الخاصة برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أثر بيان هدايته العامة

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r4.claim: This guidance enables the Prophet to receive and preserve revelation, the Quran that guides the worlds, and to guide all people.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r4.anchor: لتلقى الوحي وحفظ القرآن الذي هو هدى للعالمين

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r5.claim: Al-Raghib reads the promise as God's assurance that the Prophet will not forget the truth he hears.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r5.anchor: في المفردات أخبار وضمان من الله تعالى أن يجعله

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r6.claim: The future particle either intensifies the promise or indicates recitation of revelation now and in the future.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r6.anchor: والسين إما للتأكيد وإما لأن المراد إقراء ما أوحى إليه حينئذ

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r7.claim: The verb aqraʾa means to teach someone and make him a reciter; Taj al-maṣādir glosses iqraʾ as keeping the Quran in the ear and making a reader.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r7.anchor: وأقرأه غيره فهو مقرىء أي علمه إياه فهو معلم

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r8.claim: Gabriel will recite what is revealed now and later, and the Prophet's strong, exact memory will prevent forgetting.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r8.anchor: سنقرئك ما نوحي إليك الآن وفيما بعد على لسانه جبرائيل

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r9.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r9.claim: The Quran will be gathered in the Prophet's heart and its recitation on his tongue, as in 75:17.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r9.anchor: سنجمع حفظ القرآن في قلبك وقراءته في لسانك حتى لا تنسى

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r10.claim: The exception is from the broadest class of objects: he will forget nothing that is recited except what God wills.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r10.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من أعم المفاعيل أي لا تنسى شيئا من الأشياء

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r11.claim: One reading is permanent forgetting of material whose recitation was abrogated, as abrogation erases it from pages and hearts.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r11.anchor: فإن النسخ نوع منا ساء وطريق من طرقه

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, the exception allows rare ordinary lapses followed by recollection, rather than permanent forgetting.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r12.anchor: النسيان المتعارف الذي يعقبه الذكر بعده وهو النسيان في الجملة

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r13.claim: A report says the Prophet omitted a verse in prayer; Ubayy thought it abrogated, and the Prophet clarified the omission.
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r13.anchor: أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة فحسب أبي رضي الله عنه إنه نسخت

BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314#2/r14.claim: The Prophet's answer to Ubayy follows his question about the omitted verse.

QASHANI:87:6-10/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:6-10/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:6-10/r1.claim: The Prophet reads the universal Quran of realities written in his book of preparedness, the Quranic intellect, and recalls it without forgetting.
QASHANI:87:6-10/r1.anchor: نجعلك قارئا لما في كتاب استعدادك الذي هو العقل القرآني

QASHANI:87:6-10/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:6-10/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:6-10/r2.claim: The exception allows God to make the Prophet forget or lose awareness of something, reserving it for his praiseworthy station at resurrection.
QASHANI:87:6-10/r2.anchor: أن ينسيك ويذهلك عنها فيدخر للمقام المحمود إذا بعثت فيه

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r15.claim: God gathers the Quran in Muhammad's heart and preserves it so that he does not forget.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r15.anchor: سنجمع القرآن في قلبك - يا محمد - حفظا حتى لا تنسى

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r16.claim: The exception concerns material outside the duty to convey, which the Prophet may forget before conveying; God knows secret and public alike.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r16.anchor: مما لا يدخل تحت التكليف فتنساه قبل التبليغ

SULAMI:v2p389#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389#4/r1.speaker: محمد بن الحسن البغدادي
SULAMI:v2p389#4/r1.claim: Muhammad al-Baghdadi reports that Ibn Kaysan, a distinguished grammarian, attended Junayd's gathering and asked him about the verse.
SULAMI:v2p389#4/r1.anchor: كان يغشى الجنيد في مجلسه أهل النسك من أهل العلوم

SULAMI:v2p389#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389#4/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p389#4/r2.claim: Asked what the verse means, Junayd replied that the Prophet should not forget to act on revelation.
SULAMI:v2p389#4/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : لا تنسى العمل به

SULAMI:v2p389#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389#4/r3.speaker: ابن كيسان النحوي
SULAMI:v2p389#4/r3.claim: Ibn Kaysan strongly praised Junayd's answer and said he deserved to preside.
SULAMI:v2p389#4/r3.anchor: فقال : لا يفضض الله فاك ، مثلك من تصدر

FARRA:v3p256/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r8.claim: The exception does not mean God will cause the Prophet to forget anything; it resembles a conventional exception not intended to be exercised.

FARRA:v3p256/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r9.claim: In ordinary speech and oaths, an exception may be stated although the speaker intends completion and does not intend to withhold anything.
FARRA:v3p256/r9.anchor: مجاري الإيمان يستثنى فيها. ونية الحالف التمام

NAHHAS:v5p205/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r1.claim: Two analyses are reported: 'do not leave' or a prediction that the Prophet will not forget; the latter is preferred because exegetes support it.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r1.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما فلا تترك والآخر أن يكون من النسيان

NAHHAS:v5p205/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r2.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p205/r2.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet recited privately to himself so as not to forget.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في نفسه لئلا ينسى

NAHHAS:v5p205/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r3.speaker: مالك بن أنس
NAHHAS:v5p205/r3.claim: Malik explains the promise as preservation, except for what God wills.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r3.anchor: حدثني مالك بن أنس في قوله ( سنقرئك فلا تنسى ) قال تحفظ إلا ما شاء الله

NAHHAS:v5p205/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r4.claim: Both readings are declarative, not prohibitive; most linguists reject commanding someone not to forget because forgetting is beyond one's control.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r4.anchor: وهو خبر وليس بنهي ولا يجوز عند أكبر أهل اللغة أن ينهى إنسان عن أن ينسى

SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r1.claim: One view takes 'do not forget' as a negative statement that the Prophet will not forget; another takes it as a prohibition with a lengthened alif.
SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r1.anchor: قيل: هو نفي، أخبر تعالى أن نبيه عليه السلام لا ينسى

SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r2.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r2.claim: Makki rejects a prohibitive reading because one cannot prohibit what is outside a person's control.
SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r2.anchor: ومنع مكي أن يكون نهيا لأنه لا ينهى عما ليس باختياره

SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r3.claim: Makkī's objection is not decisive: the prohibition can concern avoiding the causes of forgetting, a common usage.
SAMIN-DURR:87:6/r3.anchor: إذ المعنى: النهي عن تعاطي أسباب النسيان، وهو شائع

ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r1.claim: God promises the illiterate Prophet a sign of distinction: Gabriel brings revelation, which the Prophet teaches his Companions without forgetting or needing repetition.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r1.anchor: جبريل عليه السلام ينزل عليه بالوحي وهو أمي لا يكتب كتابا ولا يقرؤه

ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r2.claim: God's preservation of the reminder supports the promise.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r2.anchor: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r1.claim: God teaches the Prophet what is taught to him so he will not forget it.
ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r1.anchor: WE SHALL teach thee, and thou wilt not forget [aught of what thou art taught]

ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r2.claim: The exception allows what God may will the Prophet to forget.
ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r2.anchor: save what God may will [thee to forget]

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:6:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:6:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:6:anmerkung/r1.claim: For qaraʾa, the reader is referred to 96:1; an imperative in verse 1 followed by a future first-person plural revelation promise also occurs in 73:2-5.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:6:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Eine analoge Aufeinanderfolge von imperativischem Aufruf (V. 1) und futurischer Offenbarungsankündigung in der 1. Person Plural (V. 6) findet sich auch in Sure 73

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r4.claim: Verse 6 shifts from third-person singular to first-person plural, a Quranic rhetorical perspective change called iltifat in Arabic.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r4.anchor: Mit V. 6 geht der Text von der 3. Person Singular in die 1. Person Plural über

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r5.speaker: Abdel Haleem
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r5.claim: Abdel Haleem argues that the shift need not reflect redaction; the first-person voice heightens the surah's authority and dramatizes it.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r5.anchor: Der Übergang zur ersten Person markiert eine deutliche Steigerung im Autoritätsanspruch der Sure

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r7.claim: The first explicit divine speaker in the surah promises the messenger further revelation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r7.anchor: Der damit erstmals in der Sure explizit auftretende göttliche Sprecher verheißt dem Verkünder

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.claim: The preceding sūrah urges the Prophet to wait: persistent deniers receive only temporary respite under God's practice, and cannot escape His grasp.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.anchor: Sūrah al-Ṭāriq, the previous sūrah ended on urging the Prophet (sws) to show patience and to wait for the decision of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.claim: This sūrah shifts its primary address from stubborn Quraysh to the Prophet and, over at least ten following sūrahs, dispels his preaching fears in varied ways.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.anchor: while ignoring these stubborn elements from among the Quraysh, the Prophet (sws) is addressed directly and given glad tidings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r4.claim: Verses 6–8 promise that revelation will mature for the Prophet, remain preserved except for what God wills to set aside, and bring ease from known hardships.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r4.anchor: The favour of revelations that he is receiving will gradually reach its culmination

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r2.claim: The gradual law seen in human development and vegetation also governs the Prophet: his prophethood and revelation will mature, and he will overcome obstacles.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r3.claim: The context matches the cautions against haste in Ṭāhā and al-Qiyāmah: revelation was the Prophet's needed support for opposition, future guidance, and answering objections, explaining his eagerness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r3.anchor: The context and occasion of the verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r1.claim: The Prophet eagerly repeated each word and wished to receive the whole revelation at once; God tells him not to hurry, since revelation follows a wise timetable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r1.anchor: would be so enthusiastic at this instance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r2.claim: God guarantees the Qur'an's preservation so the Prophet will not forget; collection, recital, following, and explanation are all assigned to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r2.anchor: Indeed, upon Us is its collection and recital. So when We have recited it out, follow this recital. Then upon Us is to explain it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r3.claim: The exception for what God pleases concerns temporary directives later abrogated; God will tell the Prophet when their term ends.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r3.anchor: The reference is to the temporary directives which were later abrogated.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says God would make His Prophet forget whatever He willed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#2/r1.anchor: قال كان الله ينسي نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم ما يشاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r7.claim: The preceding sūra called revelation decisive speech, and this sūra identifies it with God's promise to recite it to the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r7.anchor: إنه لقول فصل ، قيل: هو سنقرئك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and Mālik take the promise as meaning the Prophet should not move his tongue hastily while revelation is coming.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r2.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة ومالك: هذا في معنى لا تحرك به لسانك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r3.claim: God promises to recite revelation and preserve it for the unlettered Prophet, making this a sign of prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r3.anchor: وعده الله أن يقرئه، وأخبره أنه لا ينسى، وهذه آية للرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r4.claim: An alternative takes the promise as recitation of the sūras and the negative as emphatic reassurance; it then warns against neglecting regular review.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r4.anchor: وقيل: هذا وعد بإقراء السور، وأمر أن لا ينسى على معنى التثبيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r5.claim: The alif remains in falā tansā despite the jussive prohibition particle, to regularize the verse endings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r5.anchor: وأثبتت الألف في فلا تنسى، وإن كان مجزوما بلا التي للنهي لتعديل رؤوس الآي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r6.claim: They take the exception as what God decreed to abrogate, removing both its recitation and ruling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r6.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما: مما قضى الله نسخه، وأن ترتفع تلاوته وحكمه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God may make the Prophet forget something so that he can establish it as a practice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسيك لتسن به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r8.claim: Another view allows temporary forgetting followed by a reminder, as when the Prophet said ʿAbbād's recitation reminded him of verses in a sūra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r8.anchor: كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام، حين سمع قراءة عباد بن بشير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r9.claim: A further view interprets not forgetting as not abandoning practice, except where God abrogates the ruling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r9.anchor: فلا تنسى: أي فلا تترك العمل به إلا ما شاء الله أن تتركه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r10.speaker: الفراء وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and others treat the exception as a conventional formula, with nothing actually exempted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء وجماعة: هذا استثناء صلة في الكلام على سنة الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī adopts that view: the exception denies forgetting altogether, using rare phrasing without intending a real exception.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r11.anchor: والغرض نفي النسيان رأسا، كما يقول الرجل لصاحبه: أنت سهيمي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r12.claim: He rejects the empty-exception account as making God's exception no exception at all, unsuitable even in eloquent speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r12.anchor: وهذا لا ينبغي أن يكون في كلام الله تعالى، بل ولا في كلام فصيح.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r13.claim: He also rejects the weak proposal that lā is prohibitive and the alif remains only for rhyme.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r13.anchor: وكذلك القول بأن لا في فلا تنسى للنهي، والألف ثابتة لأجل الفاصلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r14.claim: The clear sense is that the Prophet will not forget except through abrogation, forgetting to establish a practice, or temporary forgetting followed by recall; he is protected from forgetting what he must convey.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r14.anchor: والمعنى أنه تعالى أخبر أنه سيقرئه، وأنه لا ينسى إلا ما شاء الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r1.claim: The promise follows the command to glorify because glorification requires reciting revelation; it allays the Prophet's fear of forgetting while reserving forgetfulness for a divine purpose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r1.anchor: لما أمره تعالى بالتسبيح، وكان التسبيح لا يتم إلا بقراءة ما أنزل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r1.claim: This is the Prophet's special divine guidance after the general guidance given to creatures: receiving and preserving the Qur'an and being enabled to guide humanity.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r1.anchor: سنقرئك فلا تنسى بيان لهدايته تعالى شأنه الخاصة برسوله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r2.claim: The sīn may be emphatic or promise continued revelation, with recitation now and of future revelation; God is said to recite by metonymy through Gabriel, its intermediary.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r2.anchor: والسين إما للتأكيد وإما لأن المراد اقراء ما أوحي إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r3.claim: The Prophet will not forget because of his strong retention despite being unlettered; this itself is a sign, alongside the Qur'an's inimitability and reports of unseen events.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r3.anchor: فلا تنسى أصلا من قوة الحفظ والأتقان مع أنك أمي لم تكن تدري

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r4.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r4.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq is cited for an alternative that the Prophet could read writing but could not write, becoming a reader by inspiration without instruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r4.anchor: فقد روي عن جعفر الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r5.claim: He says the inspired-reader interpretation conflicts with transmitted early explanations and with the causal fāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r5.anchor: وفيه أنه مع كونه خلاف المأثور عن السلف في الآية تأباه فاء التفريع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r6.claim: An alternative construes not forgetting as not neglecting the Qur'an's commands, a promise of compliance that al-Ālūsī regards as far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r6.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون المراد نفي نسيان المضمون أي سنقرئك القرآن فلا تغفل عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r7.claim: Reading falā tansā as a prohibition with a retained alif for rhyme is strained because forgetting is involuntary; appeals to figurative neglect or orthography also require contortions.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r7.anchor: وقيل فلا تنسى نهي والألف لمراعاة الفاصلة كما في قوله تعالى وأضلونا السبيلا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r8.speaker: الإمام المرزوقي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r8.claim: Al-Marzūqī is cited as saying that when an alif is lengthened at pause, a deleted alif is restored.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105/r8.anchor: مع أن الإمام المرزوقي صرح بأنه عند الإطلاق ترد المحذوفة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r1.claim: God will teach the Prophet through Gabriel's recitation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r2.claim: The exception means what God wills the Prophet to forget, including Qur'anic recitation whose abrogation is a kind of making one forget.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r2.anchor: أن تنساه، وما نسخ الله تلاوته من القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r3.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r3.claim: Mujāhid and al-Kalbī report that the Prophet used to begin reciting a verse before Gabriel finished it, fearing he would forget; after this reassurance he forgot nothing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد، والكلبي: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه جبريل

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r3.claim: The promise may mean reciting the Qur'an through Gabriel or inspiring the Prophet to become a reader.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r3.anchor: على لسان جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام، أو سنجعلك قارئا بإلهام القراءة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r4.claim: The Prophet will not forget because of strong memory despite illiteracy; the prediction's fulfillment is another sign of his prophethood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r4.anchor: أصلا من قوة الحفظ مع أنك أمي ليكون ذلك آية أخرى لك

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r5.claim: Another view treats falā tansā as prohibition, with the alif retained for rhyme as in the cited form al-sabīlā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r5.anchor: وقيل نهي والألف للفاصلة كقوله تعالى السبيلا

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r6.claim: The exception may refer to forgetting through abrogation of recitation; alternatively, it may signal rarity, and a report says the Prophet forgot a verse during prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r6.anchor: نسيانه بأن نسخ تلاوته، وقيل أراد به القلة والنذرة.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r2.claim: The surah's purpose is to affirm God's transcendence above every deficiency, including haste, inability to resurrect, purposeless creation, false speech, or speech humans can imitate.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r2.anchor: إيجاب التنزيه للأعلى سبحانه وتعالى عن أن يلحق ساحة عظمته شيء من شوائب النقص

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r3.claim: The surah al-Tariq alluded to these denials generally, while this surah explains them in detail.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r3.anchor: كما أذنت بذلك الطارق مجملا وشرحته هذه مفصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r5.claim: Beginning with God's essence, attributes, self-subsistence, and acts before prophethood cures ignorant imitation and arrogant denial and leads to obedience.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r7.claim: After establishing God's existence, attributes, creative power, guidance, and governance, the surah turns to the creatures and first to the Messenger receiving revelation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r7.anchor: فدل على تمام أصول الدين بالدلالة على وجوده سبحانه على سبيل التنزل من ذاته إلى صفاته ثم إلى أفعاله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r8.claim: Human flourishing requires an infallible exemplar; love for God's sake is one of religion's greatest supports.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r8.anchor: ولا مقتدي مثل المعصوم عن كل ميل الموجب ذلك الحب من كل ما يعرف حاله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r9.claim: God repeatedly makes the illiterate Prophet a reciter, fully knowledgeable in the life-giving revelation and able to spread and clarify it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r9.anchor: نجعلك بعظمتنا بوعد لا خلف فيه على سبيل التكرار بالتجديد والاستمرار قارئا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r10.claim: The promise that he will not forget anything ensures both that an unlettered man recites and that his prediction of the future comes true.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r10.anchor: ليكون في ذلك آيتان : كونك تقرأ وأنت أمي , وكونك تخبر عن المستقبل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r11.claim: The Prophet need not move his tongue hastily or exhaust himself during revelation: God preserves it in his heart and makes his tongue recite it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r11.anchor: فإن علينا حفظه في صدرك وإنطاق لسانك به

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r1.claim: The Prophet reviewed the Quran inwardly because he feared forgetting it, so God assured him that He would suffice him; the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستذكر القرآن فخافة أن ينساه فقيل له: كفيناك ذلك

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r2.claim: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas transmits a similar report about the Prophet fearing he would forget the Quran.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r2.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص نحوه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet would rehearse the Quran to himself because he feared forgetting it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : سنقرئك فلا تنسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r3.claim: The surah supports and steadies the Prophet in receiving revelation and promises him a gracious law and a book that reminds the purified and God-fearing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r3.anchor: شريعة سمحة وكتابا يتذكر به أهل النفوس الزكية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r5.claim: The revelation confirms earlier messengers' scriptures and thus comforts the Prophet amid pagan rejection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r5.anchor: وأن ما أوحي إليه يصدقه ما في كتب الرسل من قبله وذلك كله تهوين لما يلقاه من إعراض المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.claim: Proportioning and guidance suit the surah because God who fashioned the Prophet for the burdens of mission also equips him to retain revelation and grants him an easy law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.anchor: الذي يسوي خلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تسوية تلائم ما خلقه لأجله من تحمل أعباء الرسالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r3.claim: The opening command to glorify was general glad tidings; this passage makes explicit the promise to preserve every recited revelation for full delivery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r3.anchor: فهذا موقع البيان الصريح بوعده بأنه سيعصمه من نسيان ما يقرئه فيبلغه كما أوحي إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r4.claim: An authentic report says the Prophet struggled to retain revelation, moved his lips while Gabriel recited, and later recited it exactly as Gabriel had.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r4.anchor: في الصحيح عن ابن عباس : ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يعالج من التنزيل شدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r5.claim: Because the linked passage in al-Qiyamah was revealed later, this verse is an earlier promise that God will help the Prophet preserve all revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r5.anchor: نزلت بعد سورة الأعلى فقد تعين أن قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r1.claim: The promise of recitation prepares for the central promise that the Prophet will not forget and assures him that preservation will continue as the Quran grows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r1.anchor: إدماجا للإعلام بأن القرآن في تزايد مستمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r2.claim: The future marker sin confirms a coming act and, alongside an act already underway, signals that recitation will continue and renew.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r2.anchor: فالسين دالة على أن الإقراء يستمر ويتجدد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r3.claim: The shift to God's majestic first-person plural suits His direct approach to the Prophet with glad tidings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r3.anchor: والالتفات بضمير المتكلم المعظم لأن التكلم أنسب بالإقبال على المبشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r4.claim: Attributing recitation to God is a rational attribution: He creates the words being recited and commands their recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r4.anchor: وإسناد الإقراء إلى الله مجاز عقلي لأنه جاعل الكلام المقروء وآمر بإقرائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r5.claim: The statement that the Prophet will not forget is declarative in form but functions as a promise and guarantee.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r5.anchor: خبر مراد به الوعد والتكفل له بذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r6.claim: The exception means whatever God chooses for the Prophet to forget; the object of chooses is omitted in keeping with common Arabic usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r6.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا ما شاء الله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r7.claim: The first and most evident case is abrogation of recitation: God has the Prophet and community stop reciting material until they forget it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r7.anchor: أن الله إذا شاء نسخ تلاوة بعض ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمره بأن يترك قراءته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r8.speaker: عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r8.claim: Umar reports that the revealed material once included a stoning verse and a warning against disowning one's fathers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p280/r8.anchor: مثل ما روي عن عمر أنه قال : ( كان فيما أنزل الشيخ والشيخه إذا زنيا فارجموهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r1.claim: A second case is temporary human lapse, after which God provides a reminder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r1.anchor: نسيانا موقتا كشأن عوارض الحافظة البشرية ثم يقيض الله له ما يذكره به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r2.claim: Aisha reports that a man reciting at night reminded the Prophet of verses he had omitted or forgotten; on another occasion Ubayy asked whether a verse omitted in prayer had been abrogated, and the Prophet said he had forgotten.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : ( سمع النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يقرأ من الليل بالمسجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r3.claim: The statement is not a prohibition: forgetting is not subject to obligation, and treating the particle as prohibitive to explain its written alif is strained.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r3.anchor: ليس قوله : { فلا تنسى } من الخبر المستعمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r15.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r15.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and Malik ibn Anas connect the promise not to forget with the instruction in al-Qiyamah not to move the tongue hastily.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r15.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة ومالك بن أنس: هذه الآية في معنى قوله تعالى: لا تحرك به لسانك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r1.claim: Others distinguish this verse from al-Qiyamah: it promises that the Prophet will retain the revealed law and surahs and reinforces his duty to keep them in mind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r1.anchor: وقال آخرون: ليست هذه الآية في معنى تلك، وإنما هذه وعد بإقرار الشرع والسور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r2.claim: The final ya in tansā is written to match the verse endings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r2.anchor: وأثبت الياء في «تنسى» لتعديل رؤوس الآي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r3.speaker: الجنيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r3.claim: Al-Junayd interprets not forgetting as not abandoning the commands and prohibitions in revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r3.anchor: وقال الجنيد: معنى فلا تنسى، لا تترك العمل بما تضمن من أمر ونهي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r11.claim: God promises to preserve revelation so the unlettered Prophet does not lose it; this is a sign of his prophethood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r11.anchor: وعد الله أن يقرئه وأخبره أنه لا ينسى نسيانا لا يكون بعده ذكر، فتذهب الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#3/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#3/r1.claim: Muqatil says God will teach the Prophet the Quran and gather it in his heart so that he will never forget it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#3/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل سنعلمك القرآن ونجمعه في قلبك فلا تنساه أبدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir selects al-Tabari’s view: God promises Muhammad a recitation he will retain, apart from what God wills.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the Messenger never forgot anything except what God willed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا إلا ما شاء الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r3.claim: An alternative takes the wording as a prohibition: do not forget what is recited, except what God abrogates, which may then be left.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: المراد بقوله: {فلا تنسى} طلب، وجعلوا معنى الاستثناء على هذا ما يقع من النسخ

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r11.claim: Iqraʾ means to take a reading by listening so as to correct mistakes; qirāʾah is recitation and is related to gathering letters together.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r11.anchor: والإقراء: أخذ القراءة على القارئ بالاستماع لتقويم الزلل، والقراءة: التلاوة، وأصله الجمع

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r1.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r1.claim: Abu Ali treats forgetfulness as an act created by God.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r1.anchor: والنسيان معنى من فعل الله تعالى، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r2.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r2.claim: Abu Hashim instead defines it as loss of ordinarily necessary knowledge, not as an entity or act.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو ذهاب العلم الضروري بما جرت به العادة أن يعلمه، وليس بمعنى، عن أبي هاشم.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r6.speaker: author
