JISHUMI:v10p7373/r6.claim: Fala tansa may be indicative information that Muhammad will not forget, or a jussive prohibition against forgetting.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r6.anchor: (فلا تنسى) قيل: محله رفع؛ لأنه خبر وليس بنهي، يعني فلست تنسى، وقيل: جزم؛ لأنه نهي.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r7.claim: The occasion report says Muhammad used to start the next verse before finishing the one being revealed, fearing he would forget; afterward he forgot nothing.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r7.anchor: قيل: كان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إذا أنزل عليه القرآن لم يفرغ من آخر الآية حتى يقرأ أولها

KASHSHAF:87:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:6/r1.claim: God gives Muhammad a clear sign: although unlettered, he hears Gabriel recite revelation and retains it without forgetting.
KASHSHAF:87:6/r1.anchor: بشره الله بإعطاء آية بينة ، وهي : أن يقرأ عليه جبريل ما يقرأ عليه من الوحي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r2.claim: One interpretation says do not forget means do not abandon the work, except what God permits as a concession; on this reading it prohibits shirk.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أن معنى قوله : فلا تنسى , أي فلا تترك العمل إلا ما شاء الله أن يترخص لك فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r3.claim: A second interpretation treats the phrase as God’s declaration that Muhammad will not forget the Qur’an He recites.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r3.anchor: والوجه الثاني : أنه إخبار من الله تعالى أنه لا ينسى ما يقرئه من القرآن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that Muhammad repeated Gabriel’s revelation for fear of forgetting it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r4.anchor: حكى ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا نزل عليه جبريل بالوحي يقرؤه خيفة أن ينساه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r5.claim: They take except what God wills to mean what He wills to abrogate, so it is forgotten.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r5.anchor: أحدهما : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسخه فتنساه , قاله الحسن وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r6.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r6.claim: Ibn Isa instead says God may delay a revelation so Muhammad has not yet recited it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r6.anchor: الثاني : إلا ما شاء الله أن يؤخر إنزاله عليك فلا تقرؤه , حكاه ابن عيسى .

MUJAHID:v2p752/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p752/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p752/r1.claim: Mujahid says Muhammad used to rehearse the Qur’an inwardly for fear of forgetting, so God assured him that He would make him recite and he would not forget.
MUJAHID:v2p752/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتذكر القرآن في نفسه مخافة أن ينسى فقال الله عز وجل

MUQATIL:87:1-7/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r6.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r6.claim: God gathers the Qur’an in Muhammad’s heart so he never forgets it, except what God wills to abrogate and replace with something better.
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r6.anchor: قوله: { سنقرئك } القرآن يا محمد نجمعه في قلبك { فلا تنسى } [آية: 6] فلا تنساه أبدا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#6/r1.claim: God will teach Muhammad the Qur’an until he does not forget it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ سنقرئك فلا تنسى ﴾ سنعلمك القرآن حتى لا تنساه

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r1.claim: The phrase means God will teach Muhammad the Qur’an so he memorizes it; Ibn Wahb transmits this interpretation from Malik.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { سنقرئك } أي القرآن يا محمد فنعلمكه { فلا تنسى } أي فتحفظ رواه ابن وهب عن مالك.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r2.claim: This is glad tidings of a clear sign: an unlettered Prophet hears Gabriel recite revelation and retains it without forgetting.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r2.anchor: وهذه بشرى من الله تعالى بشره بأن أعطاه آية بينة، وهي أن يقرأ عليه جبريل ما يقرأ عليه من الوحي

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r3.claim: Mujahid says Muhammad repeated revelation to himself for fear of forgetting, then was told he was spared that worry.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r3.anchor: وعن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد، قال: كان يتذكر مخافة أن ينسى، فقيل: كفيتكه.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r4.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r4.claim: They say Muhammad would begin an ayah before Gabriel finished it, fearing he would forget; thereafter he forgot nothing because God took care of it.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد والكلبي: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه جبريل بالوحي، لم يفرغ جبريل من آخر الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r5.claim: Al-Farra says the exception is a formal qualification with no intended forgotten item, as in the promise that the righteous will remain in Heaven unless God wills otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r5.anchor: ووجه الاستثناء على هذا، ما قاله الفراء: إلا ما شاء الله، وهو لم يشأ أن تنسى شيئا كقوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r6.claim: Abu Salih transmits Ibn Abbas’s report that Muhammad forgot nothing after the verse came down until he died, apart from what God willed.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r6.anchor: وفي رواية أبي صالح عن ابن عباس: فلم ينس بعد نزول هذه الآية حتى مات

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r7.claim: Saʿid transmits Qatadah’s report that the Messenger forgot nothing except what God willed.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r7.anchor: وعن سعيد عن قتادة، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r8.claim: One explanation allows a temporary lapse followed by recollection; a report says Muhammad omitted an ayah in prayer, Ubay thought it abrogated, and Muhammad said he had forgotten it.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r8.anchor: وقيل: إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسى، ثم يذكر بعد ذلك فإذا قد نسي، ولكنه يتذكر ولا ينسى نسيانا كليا.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r9.claim: Forget may mean that God causes Muhammad to forget what He abrogates; exception is then a kind of abrogation of recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r9.anchor: ثم قيل: هذا بمعنى النسخ أي إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسخه. والاستثناء نوع من النسخ.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r10.claim: Another reading makes forgetting mean abandoning practice: God protects him from leaving the teaching except where He abrogates its application.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r10.anchor: وقيل: النسيان بمعنى الترك أي يعصمك من أن تترك العمل به إلا ما شاء الله أن تتركه لنسخه إياه.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r11.speaker: الجنيد
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r11.claim: Al-Junayd answers that you will not forget means you will not neglect acting on the teaching; Ibn Kaysan praises the answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r11.anchor: لا تنسى العمل به. فقال ابن كيسان: لا يفضض الله فاك! مثلك من يصدر عن رأيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r12.claim: The particle fa may be negation rather than prohibition; another view takes it as prohibition, with yāʾ retained for the verse ending.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:6-7/r12.anchor: وقوله: «فلا»: للنفي لا للنهي. وقيل: للنهي وإنما أثبتت الياء لأن رؤوس الآي على ذلك.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r1.claim: God relieves Muhammad of the burden of retaining the Qur’an by guaranteeing its preservation in his heart; Muhammad had been driven by love and responsibility to repeat each verse and move his tongue for fear of losing even a letter.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r1.anchor: وتبدأ البشرى برفع عناء الحفظ لهذا القرآن والكد في إمساكه عن عاتق الرسول

QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r2.claim: The assurance comforts the Prophet and, through him, his community: the faith originates with God, who guards it in the Prophet’s heart.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r2.anchor: وهي بشرى لأمته من ورائه ، تطمئن بها إلى أصل هذه العقيدة . فهي من الله . والله كافلها وحافظها في قلب نبيها .

QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r3.claim: The exception affirms that God’s will remains free and unconfined even when He gives a firm promise or establishes a lasting law.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r3.anchor: وفي هذا الموضع كما في كل موضع يرد فيه وعد جازم ، أو ناموس دائم ، يرد ما يفيد طلاقة المشيئة الإلهية

QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r4.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly emphasizes that divine will remains unrestricted behind its promises and laws.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:6/r4.anchor: ويحرص القرآن على تقرير هذه الحقيقة في كل موضع - كما سبق أن مثلنا لهذا في الظلال

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r1.claim: Because complete glorification includes reciting the Qur’an God revealed, Muhammad rehearsed it from fear of forgetting; this verse removes that fear.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r1.anchor: وعلم محمدا عليه السلام أن ذلك التسبيح لا يتم ولا يكمل إلا بقراءة ما أنزله الله تعالى عليه من القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r2.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi explains sanuqriʾuka as God making Muhammad a reader by inspiring him, so he will not forget what he reads.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي : { سنقرئك } أي سنجعلك قارئا بأن نلهمك القراءة فلا تنسى

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r3.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل والكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r3.claim: They say Muhammad moved his tongue quickly during revelation, before Gabriel finished, because he feared forgetting; God promised to teach him until he retained the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد ومقاتل والكلبي : كان عليه السلام إذا نزل عليه القرآن أكثر تحريك لسانه مخافة أن ينسى

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r4.claim: One explanation is that Gabriel will repeat the recitation until Muhammad memorizes it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r4.anchor: أحدها : أن جبريل عليه السلام سيقرأ عليك القرآن مرات حتى تحفظه حفظا لا تنساه

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r5.claim: A second explanation is that God strengthens Muhammad so he memorizes after one hearing.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r5.anchor: وثانيها : أنا نشرح صدرك ونقوي خاطرك حتى تحفظ بالمرة الواحدة حفظا لا تنساه

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r6.claim: A third explanation links the promise to the Qur’an’s comprehensive knowledge and to making the work of acting on it easy.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r6.anchor: وثالثها : أنه تعالى لما أمره في أول السورة بالتسبيح فكأنه تعالى قال : واظب على ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r7.claim: The verse demonstrates a miracle: an unlettered man memorized an extensive book without study, repetition, or writing.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r7.anchor: أنه كان رجلا أميا فحفظه لهذا الكتاب المطول من غير دراسة ولا تكرار ولا كتبة

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r8.claim: Because the verse came early in the Meccan period, its prediction that this extraordinary event would occur and then did occur is another miracle of foreknowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r8.anchor: من أوائل ما نزل بمكة ، فهذا إخبار عن أمر عجيب

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r9.claim: One view reads fala tansa as a prohibition with an added alif for the verse ending, meaning do not neglect recitation and repetition; the famous view reads it as a promise that Muhammad will be safe from forgetting.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r9.anchor: قال بعضهم : { فلا تنسى } معناه النهي ، والألف مزيدة للفاصلة ، كقوله

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r10.claim: Al-Razi prefers the declarative promise that God makes Muhammad secure from forgetting, like promising clothing so someone will not be naked.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r10.anchor: والقول المشهور أن هذا خبر والمعنى سنقرئك إلى أن تصير بحيث لا تنسى وتأمن النسيان

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r11.claim: He rejects the prohibition reading because it requires extra constructions, treats forgetfulness as something Muhammad can avoid only by ordinary effort, weakens the divine glad tidings, and conflicts with 75:16.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r11.anchor: واحتج أصحاب هذا القول على ضعف القول الأول بأن ذلك القول لا يتم إلا عند التزام مجازات في هذه الآية منها أن النسيان لا يقدر عليه إلا الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r1.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says Muhammad did not forget anything after the verse was revealed; on this view the exception is not actual.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي : إنه عليه السلام لم ينس بعد نزول هذه الآية شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r2.claim: The non-actual exception may teach the formula if God wills, even when God knows what will happen, as in the command not to promise a future act without it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r2.anchor: التبرك بذكر هذه الكلمة على ما قال تعالى : { ولا تقولن لشىء إنى فاعل ذالك غدا * إلا أن يشاء الله }

RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r3.claim: Al-Farra says God did not will Muhammad to forget, but the exception demonstrates that He could; preservation is God’s favor, not Muhammad’s own power.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r3.anchor: قال الفراء : إنه تعالى ما شاء أن ينسى محمد عليه السلام شيئا ، إلا أن المقصود

RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r4.claim: The exception may keep Muhammad vigilant, since he remains attentive about whether any portion of revelation is the one excluded.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r4.anchor: جوز رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كل ما ينزل عليه من الوحي قليلا كان أو كثيرا أن يكون ذلك هو المستثنى

RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r5.claim: A final non-actual reading treats the exception as rhetorical, with no intention to exclude anything.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r5.anchor: أن يكون الغرض من قوله : { إلا ما شاء الله } نفي النسيان رأسا

RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r6.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows a temporary lapse followed by recollection; a report says Muhammad omitted an ayah in prayer, Ubay thought it abrogated, and Muhammad said he had forgotten it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسى ، فإنه ينسى ثم يتذكر بعد ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r7.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r7.claim: Maqatil takes forget as abrogation: a verse God wills to abrogate is no longer recited or used in prayer and eventually leaves memory.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسيه ، ويكون المراد من الإنساء ههنا نسخه

RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r8.claim: Another interpretation allows only a rare lapse of etiquette or sunnah, not an obligation, since forgetting a required ruling would damage the law.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129/r8.anchor: القلة والندرة ، ويشترط أن لا يكون ذلك القليل من واجبات الشرع

STUDYQURAN:87:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:6/r1.claim: The verse assures the Prophet that God grants revelation in due time and preserves it in his memory.
STUDYQURAN:87:6/r1.anchor: This verse is an assurance that God will grant revelation in due time

STUDYQURAN:87:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:6/r2.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:6/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet sometimes recited the beginning before Gabriel finished, fearing he would forget; then this verse was revealed.
STUDYQURAN:87:6/r2.anchor: the Prophet would sometimes recite the beginning of the passage being revealed before Gabriel had finished

STUDYQURAN:87:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:6/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:6/r3.claim: In 20:114 and 75:16–17 the Prophet is also counseled not to hasten revelation.
STUDYQURAN:87:6/r3.anchor: In 20:114 and 75:16–17, the Prophet is also counseled not to “hasten”

TAB:87:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:6/r1.claim: One view says God teaches and preserves the Quran for Muhammad while forbidding haste, as in 75:16–17.
TAB:87:6/r1.anchor: سنقرئك يا محمد هذا القرآن فلا تنساه ، إلا ما شاء الله

TAB:87:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:6/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:87:6/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet mentally rehearsed the Quran for fear of forgetting.
TAB:87:6/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قوله :  سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسَى قال :  كان يتذكر القرآن في نفسه مخافة أن ينسى

TAB:87:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:6/r3.speaker: قائلو هذه المقالة
TAB:87:6/r3.claim: One group says the exception means forgetting material whose recitation and ruling God abrogates.
TAB:87:6/r3.anchor: فقال قائلو هذه المقالة :  معنى الاستثناء في هذا الموضع على النسيان

TAB:87:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:6/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:6/r4.claim: Qatādah says the Prophet forgot nothing except what God willed.
TAB:87:6/r4.anchor: عن قتادة سنقرئك فلا تنسى كان صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا إلا ما شاء الله

TAB:87:6/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:6/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB:87:6/r5.claim: Others take forgetting to mean abandoning practice: the Prophet will not leave revelation unacted upon except where God abrogates it.
TAB:87:6/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون :  معنى النسيان في هذا الموضع :  الترك وقالوا :  معنى الكلام

TAB:87:6/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:6/r6.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:87:6/r6.claim: Some grammarians take the exception rhetorically: God does not intend the Prophet to forget, like conventional exceptions meant to withhold nothing.
TAB:87:6/r6.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يقول في ذلك :  لم يشأ الله أن تنسى شيئا

TAB:87:6/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:6/r7.speaker: author
TAB:87:6/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that God only causes forgetting by abrogating and withdrawing revelation.
TAB:87:6/r7.anchor: والقول الذي هو أولى بالصواب عندي ، قول من قال :  معنى ذلك :  فلا تنسى

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r5.speaker: المفردات
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r5.claim: Al-Mufradāt defines reading as joining letters and words in measured recitation, not every kind of gathering or uttering a single letter.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r5.anchor: قال في المفردات والقراءة ضم الحروف والكلمات بعضها إلى بعض في الترتيل

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r6.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r6.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines making someone recite as listening in order to correct errors; a qāriʾ is a reciter.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r6.anchor: وقال في المجمع والإقراء أخذ القراءة على القارئ بالاستماع لتقويم الزلل

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r7.claim: God's teaching the Prophet to recite does not mean correcting him; there is no known case of him misreading or forgetting revelation and being corrected.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r7.anchor: فلم يعهد من النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يقرأ شيئا من القرآن فلا يحسنه

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r8.claim: Rather, God enables him to recite exactly as revealed without addition, omission, or distortion from forgetfulness.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r8.anchor: المراد تمكينه من قراءة القرآن كما أنزل من غير أن يغيره بزيادة أو نقص

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r9.claim: The exception preserves God's unlimited power to cause forgetting after granting protected recitation, though He will not do so.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r9.anchor: استثناء مفيد لبقاء القدرة الإلهية على إطلاقها وأن هذه العطية وهي الإقراء

TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r1.claim: The verse supports the report that the Prophet hurried to repeat Gabriel's revelation for fear of forgetting; afterward, he forgot nothing.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r1.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذا نزل عليه جبريل بالوحي يقرؤه مخافة أن ينساه

TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r2.claim: A plausible order is 87:6, then 75:16–19, followed by 20:114, all addressing haste in receiving revelation.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r2.anchor: ثم قوله لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه

TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r4.claim: God's knowledge of the manifest and hidden explains the guarantee because He knows the Prophet's concern for revelation and obedience.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r4.anchor: والجملة في مقام التعليل لقوله. { سنقرئك فلا تنسى } والمعنى سنصلح لك بالك

TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r5.claim: The shift to third-person ‘He knows’ points to divine power as the basis of the exception.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r5.anchor: التفات من التكلم مع الغير إلى الغيبة والنكتة فيه الإشارة إلى حجة الاستثناء

THALABI:v10p184/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184/r1.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p184/r1.claim: Mujāhid and al-Kalbī say the Prophet recited revelation's beginning before Gabriel finished, fearing forgetfulness; afterward he forgot nothing.
THALABI:v10p184/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد والكلبي: كان النبي (عليه السلام) إذا نزل جبريل بالقرآن

THALABI:v10p184/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184/r2.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p184/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the exception means God did not intend the Prophet to forget, like conventional exceptions meant to withhold nothing.
THALABI:v10p184/r2.anchor: ووجه الاستثناء على هذا التأويل ما قاله الفراء: لم يشأ أن ينسى شيئا

THALABI:v10p184/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184/r3.speaker: الجنيد
THALABI:v10p184/r3.claim: Al-Junayd answers Ibn Kaysān that the Prophet will not forget to act on revelation; Ibn Kaysān praises the answer.
THALABI:v10p184/r3.anchor: لا تنسى العمل به، فأعجب ابن كيسان به إعجابا شديدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r1.claim: God makes the Prophet a reader by inspiring recitation, so he does not forget what he reads.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r1.anchor: أي سنجعلك قارئا بأن نلهمك القراءة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq calls this a sign of distinction: Gabriel teaches an unlettered man revelation that he recites without forgetting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحق: أعلم الله أنه سيجعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r3.claim: The source says Qatādah holds the same view of preserved recitation despite the Prophet's illiteracy.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r4.claim: Mujāhid, Muqātil, and al-Kalbī report the Prophet repeatedly moved his tongue as revelation came for fear of forgetting, reciting before Gabriel finished.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r5.claim: The promise recalls commands not to hasten revelation in 20:114 and 75:16.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p438/r5.anchor: وهذا كقوله: {ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى

WAHIDI-QT:87:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:6/r1.claim: God promises to make the Prophet a reader of Gabriel's revelation and preserve it so that he forgets none of it.
WAHIDI-QT:87:6/r1.anchor: { سنقرئك } سنجعلك قارئا لما يأتيك به جبريل عليه السلام من الوحي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r6.claim: God promises preserved recitation of Gabriel's revelation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r6.anchor: { سنقرئك } سنجعلك قارئا لما يأتيك به جبريل عليه السلام

ELMALILI:87:6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r1.claim: He renders the promise as God henceforth teaching the Prophet to recite the Qur’an, so he will not forget it.
ELMALILI:87:6/r1.anchor: Bundan böyle sana Kur’an [5737] okutacağız da unutmayacaksın

ELMALILI:87:6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r2.claim: Because the Prophet had not known scripture or reading, Gabriel, the Trustworthy Spirit and Holy Spirit, would reveal and teach him the Qur’an and enable its recitation; Elmalılı links this to 42:52.
ELMALILI:87:6/r2.anchor: sen kitab nedir, okumak nedir bilmezken bundan böyle Rûh-i Emîn, Rûhu’l-Kudüs olan Cibrîl vâsıtasıyla sana okuyacağın bir kitap olan Kur’ân’ı vahyederek indirip belleteceğiz

ELMALILI:87:6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r3.claim: Alternatively, revelation makes the Prophet a possessor of the Qur’an and recitation.
ELMALILI:87:6/r3.anchor: Yahut vahiy ile seni Kur’an ve kıraat sâhibi yapacağız.

ELMALILI:87:6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r4.claim: This extraordinary guidance and divine prophethood is a sign and miracle.
ELMALILI:87:6/r4.anchor: bu fevkalâde hidâyet ve risâlet-i ilâhiyeye delâlet eyleyen bir âyet, bir mucize olacak

ELMALILI:87:6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r5.claim: The Prophet’s powerful retention is another sign.
ELMALILI:87:6/r5.anchor: Bu unutmamak, bu derece kuvvetli bir hıfza sâhip olmak da diğer bir âyet ve mucize olacak

ELMALILI:87:6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r6.claim: The foretold promise and its later fulfillment are themselves another miracle.
ELMALILI:87:6/r6.anchor: Nitekim bunun istikbal için va‘d ü ihbârı ve öylece vukū‘u da ayrıca bir mucize olacaktır.

ELMALILI:87:6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r7.claim: The promise to make him recite means teaching him to recite from memory, not reading a text before him.
ELMALILI:87:6/r7.anchor: Bu delâlet eder ki okutmaktan murad ezbere okutmaktır. Yoksa yüzüne yazı okumak değildir.

ELMALILI:87:6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r8.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:87:6/r8.claim: Some say that not forgetting means acting according to the Qur’an’s commands.
ELMALILI:87:6/r8.anchor: Bazıları da demişlerdir[^3] ki unutmamaktan asıl murad, mûcebiyle amel etmektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r1.claim: Early in revelation, the Prophet hurried to memorize, repeating a word or letter before Gabriel finished for fear of missing it; the author links 87:6’s descent with the command and reassurance in 75:16–19.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber ilk dönemlerde kendisine gelen Kur’an vahyini ezberleme konusunda oldukça aceleci davranıyor, bir kelime veya harfi kaçırma korkusuyla Cebrâil vahyi henüz tamamlamadan tekrar etmeye çalışıyordu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r2.claim: The revelation both stopped the Prophet’s haste and assured him that the revelation would be preserved.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r2.anchor: Böylece bir taraftan Hz. Peygamber bu davranışından vazgeçirilmiş oluyor, diğer taraftan da vahyin korunmasının güvenceye alındığı bildiriliyordu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r3.claim: Protection from forgetting is a proof of God’s power; the miracle in the Prophet continues to appear in the community’s ability to read and memorize the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r3.anchor: Peygamberin şahsında gerçekleşen bu ilâhî mûcizenin sırrı, Kur’an’ı okuma ve ezberleme tarzında ümmetin hafızalarında sürekli olarak tecelli etmektedir.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#3/r1.claim: Al-Tabarani reports from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, fearing he would forget, began repeating the revelation while Gabriel was still delivering it; the verse was then revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه جبريل بالوحي لم يفرغ جبريل من الوحي حتى يتكلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأوله مخافة ان ينساه

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#3/r2.speaker: author
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228#3/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti notes that the report’s chain contains Juwaybir, whom he rates very weak.

DURR:87:7/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:7/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:87:7/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet would rehearse the Qur’an inwardly because he feared forgetting it.
DURR:87:7/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : { سنقرئك فلا تنسى } قال : كان يتذكر القرآن في نفسه

DURR:87:7/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:7/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:7/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet began repeating Gabriel’s recitation from fear of forgetting; Gabriel told him no earlier prophet escaped forgetting or having some revelation lifted, and Moses lost four of thirteen scrolls when his emerald tablets broke.
DURR:87:7/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه جبريل بالوحي

DURR:87:7/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:7/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:7/r3.claim: A second Ibn Abbas report says the Prophet reviewed the Qur’an for fear of forgetting, then was told that God would ensure its retention.
DURR:87:7/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستذكر القرآن مخافة أن ينساه

DURR:87:7/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:7/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
DURR:87:7/r4.claim: Al-Suyuti cites Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas as relating a similar account of the Prophet’s concern about forgetting the Qur’an.
DURR:87:7/r4.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص نحوه .
